Lessons.Title: Equivalent Decimals
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: You will reason about equivalent tenths and hundredths in decimal notation.
Key idea: Equivalent decimals may have trailing zeroes without changing value, and hundredths must not be confused with tenths.
How to reason: Express each decimal as tenths or hundredths before deciding whether two notations name the same quantity.
Source-inspired opening: Warm-up:  True or False: Equivalent Fractions	 (10 minutes). Use the teacher-provided mathematical representations and explain how different valid answers arise.

Activity 1:  Card Sort: Diagrams of Fractions and Decimals	 (15 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as Your teacher will give you a set of cards. Each large square on the cards represents 1., Are 0.20 and 0.2 equivalent? Use fractions and a diagram to explain your reasoning.. First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 2:  True or Not True?	 (20 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\frac{50}{100} = 0.50\), \(0.05 = 0.5\), \(0.3 = \frac{3}{10}\), \(0.3 = \frac{30}{100}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.
